The sequence of clamp application during open abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) surgery does not appear to significantly affect the number of emboli detected when the first vascular clamp is applied to the proximal aorta or iliacs. This suggests that the initial application of clamps may not have a substantial impact on distal embolisation, which refers to the blockage of smaller blood vessels in the body.

In other words, the presence and timing of the first vascular clamp do not seem to influence the formation of emboli at the distal level of the aorta. This finding is important because it can help guide surgical procedures and patient care in this complex and high-risk surgery.

It's worth noting that while the initial application of clamps may not significantly affect distal embolisation, other factors such as the technique used to apply the clamps, the overall surgical approach, and individual patient factors (e.g., anatomy and physiology) can still play a role in determining the risk of distal embolisation.
